deleted.text: That wicket gave Crestview a real opening, because Ryan Cole was soon run out and Logan Shaw followed after a brief stay, leaving Harborfield at 133 for 4 and suddenly close enough to uncertainty for the fielding side to believe the innings might still be dragged back.

His unbeaten 101 from 88 balls carried the innings from repair to command, and by the time Harborfield closed on 252 for 8 from 36 overs, the score had a full shape: Rowe and Marsh building the road, Noah becoming the axis, Vale supplying the decisive middle support, and the lower order keeping the last section alive enough to prevent the finish from flattening.

Lucas Grant took the first wicket, Zach Foster removed Marsh and Connor Wells, Aaron Shaw broke the small Logan stand, Nathan Cole fought hard through the expensive sections, and Dylan Price kept running in, but the extras and the inability to separate Noah from the innings meant the target became far too large.

The toss gave them that option, Harborfield chose to bat, and the first few overs had the usual youth-cricket mixture of neat new-ball carry, ring-field chatter, and small mistakes that look harmless until the innings has already grown beyond control.
